REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell) -> u2
(u0, holding_box) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u3
(u1, box_fell) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, holding_box) -> u1
(u2, !holding_box & !box_fell) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box, u1) -> 0.1
(u2, holding_box, u1) -> 0.2
(u1, at_exit & holding_box, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. Format matches the required paper layout exactly (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers, arrow syntax, ordered per-state rules each closed by an else clause). FINAL_STATES is nonempty (u3), declared in STATES, and accepting: it is entered only via (u1, at_exit & holding_box), exactly this task's success condition, mirroring the environment's require=['holding_box'] exit payment. Reachability: u0 initial, u1 via first pickup, u2 via a fall from u1, u3 via exit-with-box; all states reachable. Determinism and ordered coverage hold: box_fell and holding_box never co-occur, at_exit never co-occurs with box_fell, and the u2 guards are mutually exclusive, so the prioritized rules are conflict-free and complete. Irrelevant events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled, no-op steps) are absorbed by per-state else self-loops in every state, as required. Persistent/event distinction is correct: box_fell is treated as a one-step event (u1->u2) and explicitly excluded in u2's guard, holding_box (persistent) drives pickup transitions, at_exit appears only in the terminal rule. The one-step recovery window is encoded well: u2 lives for exactly one step after a fall, so (u2, holding_box) -> u1 with reward 0.2 fires only when the pickup happens on the very next move; a missed deadline forfeits the bonus and routes to u1 so the machine never traps the agent — a defensible soft encoding of 'very next move', since a hard latched failure would be unsatisfiable whenever the box lands to the agent's side or behind (a turn must precede the pickup), and the environment's own payment does not gate on recovery timing. Reward safety: non-negative, bounded (max 0.1 + 2x0.2 + 1.0 = 1.5, since at most two falls can fire), attached only to declared transitions, with no spurious penalty for the agent-uncontrollable scheduled fall; progress rewards (0.1 pickup, 0.2 recovery) are dense toward the bounded 1.0 terminal. Regressions are explicit where the task requires them (u1->u2 on the fall, u2->u1 on recovery). Compactness is good: four states with distinct roles (pre-pickup, carrying, one-step recovery window, success); no state could be merged without changing the reward semantics. Two minor notes, not disqualifying: (1) the transition (u0, box_fell) -> u2 is dead code — a fall can only fire after a pickup, and the pickup step already moves the machine to u1 — it carries no reward and is harmless, but could be dropped; (2) the 'very next move' requirement is enforced through the 0.2 differential rather than a lapsed/failure state, which is reasonable given the landing geometry, but worth documenting as a design choice.
